delete.description: One transaction decides the whole selection: every file is committed to deletion and every folder removed, or nothing changes. Without `recursive`, a selected folder must hold nothing but uploads abandoned for 10 minutes, which are deleted with it (`FOLDER_NOT_EMPTY` otherwise). With `recursive: true`, everything inside goes too, at most 200 items besides the selected folders themselves, selected files included (`SELECTION_TOO_LARGE`). An item inside another selected folder is dropped from the selection. Refused while a record references a file (`FILE_IN_USE`), while a file is changing visibility (`FILE_BUSY`), or while an upload younger than 10 minutes is in a folder (`FOLDER_BUSY`); each names what blocked it in `data`. An `own`-scoped grant reaches only what the caller created or uploaded: a folder or an active file someone else made answers 404 and deletes nothing, while an upload in progress or abandoned counts as above whoever started it. `folderIds` lists every deleted folder, descendants included; `deleted` and `pending` split the files as on the file-only route.

files.description: The file, for the record named by `resource` and `purpose`. Exactly one file. Images (image/png, image/webp, image/svg+xml): at most 1 MiB, 25,000,000 decoded pixels and 16,383 pixels on either edge; PNG is re-encoded to WebP, SVG is sanitised. Documents (application/pdf, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet): at most 10 MiB, byte-inspected: macro-enabled, template, encrypted and object-embedding variants are refused; field codes, external links and DDE are not inspected, and documents are always served as attachments, never rendered. Upload several files as sequential single-file requests with bounded concurrency and honour `Retry-After` on 429.

inUse.description: Whether any record references the file; such a file cannot be deleted.

transition.description: Non-null while a visibility change is in flight, and each value tells a client something different: `to_public`/`to_private` mean the copy is being made and verified and `url` still answers from the OLD bucket, so the change is in progress; `cleanup` means the flip is done and `url` is final, and only the stale copy in the other bucket (and, for a public one, its edge cache) is still being removed by the nightly sweep — nothing is pending for the client. `url` always points at the current bucket. Removing the object from the origin is unconditional; evicting an edge copy needs the configured cache purge; a copy already in a browser stays readable until its `Cache-Control` lifetime ends and cannot be recalled.

unfiledAt.description: When the nightly sweep first found the file unfiled — active, in no folder, referenced by no record. It is deleted `retentionDays` (see `scope=unfiled`) after this unless moved into a folder; null otherwise.

uploadedByName.description: Null once that account is deleted.

url.description: Permanent public URL for a public object. Otherwise a signed URL that stays the same for 10 minutes and is valid for 60 to 70 minutes, which a private image's response lets the browser cache for those 10 minutes. Never store it.
